description: Somos uma equipe movida pela curiosidade, criatividade e inovação. Acreditamos que grandes descobertas começam com pequenas ideias e que a tecnologia é uma ferramenta poderosa para transformar o futuro. Nosso objetivo é explorar possibilidades, superar desafios e desenvolver soluções inteligentes para problemas reais, conectando ciência, tecnologia e criatividade.
summary:
It is an educational space exploration game that aims to reveal a little-known chapter of human history: the legacy of machines sent into space that remained on the Moon, on Mars, and on other celestial bodies.

Through an interactive experience of exploration and investigation, players navigate space environments, locate real equipment like rovers, probes, and landing modules, and discover their stories, functions, challenges, and contributions to science. Each discovery connects the player to historical missions and shows how these technologies helped expand our knowledge of the universe.

The project turns historical and scientific information into an accessible and engaging experience, using exploration, interaction, and free discovery, without relying on traditional classes or mandatory questions. Its content is based on real information from space missions, combining education, technology, and entertainment.

More than just showcasing forgotten equipment, SPACE RELICS aims to preserve its legacy, spark scientific curiosity, and inspire new generations to understand and take part in the future of space exploration.
details:
What does the project do and how does it work?

SPACE RELICS is an educational space exploration game set in the year 2085. The player takes on the role of an explorer responsible for investigating the traces of human missions scattered across the Solar System, discovering equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and other celestial bodies.

The experience combines exploring interactive environments, using a scanner, driving vehicles, and investigating objects. By finding real equipment, such as rovers, probes, and landing modules, the player can learn their stories, understand their functions, and discover their contributions to science. The game also features a Museum of Forgotten Machines, a discovery catalog, a timeline, and resources to understand space distances.

What benefits does the project offer?

The main benefit is making knowledge about space exploration more interesting, visual, and accessible. Instead of presenting scientific information only through texts or traditional explanations, the game lets people learn while they explore and investigate. This way, it brings kids, students, and space enthusiasts closer to topics like astronomy, the history of space missions, engineering, and technology.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to spark scientific curiosity, encourage interest in space exploration, and expand knowledge about equipment and missions that are often little remembered. The project also aims to highlight the technological and scientific legacy left by humanity on other celestial bodies, showing that these machines still have important stories to tell, even after their missions have ended.

What tools and technologies were used?

The prototype was developed with the help of Claude, an artificial intelligence tool used during the game’s creation and implementation process, including the development of visual elements and AI-generated 3D models. The experience was published on the Netlify platform and can be accessed directly through the browser, without the need to install any software.

How is the project creative?

The creative edge of SPACE RELICS lies in turning often-forgotten equipment into the stars of an investigative experience. Unlike ideas that focus solely on exploring new worlds, the player explores to find out what humanity has already achieved in these settings. The idea of setting the experience in 2085 also allows presenting this equipment as historical remnants from an earlier era of space exploration. This way, the game connects history, engineering, and science through curiosity and free discovery.

What factors did the team consider during development?

Our team focused on creating an intuitive, immersive, and accessible experience, mainly aimed at children and students, but that could also spark interest in other audiences. We considered ease of navigation, clarity of information, educational value, freedom of exploration, and the importance of showcasing real equipment and their stories. We also aimed to include accessibility features, such as text adjustments, color options, touch controls, and read-aloud functions, as available in the prototype.

With SPACE RELICS, we want to show that space exploration doesn’t end when a mission is over. The equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and elsewhere represents part of human history and the discoveries that brought us closer to understanding the Universe.
